messages.author: 4f6f5f995ee31178
messages.subject: Multiple PC plot with qplot or ggplot
parts:
Hi!

Can I use facet to simplify the following set of commands
qpc12 = qplot(PC1,PC2,data=spectsREFtargets20110408t2pcadf,geom="text",label=target,size=I(2),color=grupos)+
opts(legend.position = "none")
qpc13 = qplot(PC1,PC3,data=spectsREFtargets20110408t2pcadf,geom="text",label=target,size=I(2),color=grupos)+
opts(legend.position = "none")
qpc23 = qplot(PC2,PC3,data=spectsREFtargets20110408t2pcadf,geom="text",label=target,size=I(2),color=grupos)+
opts(legend.position = "none")
grid.arrange(qpc12,qpc13,qpc23,ncol=2)

I've tried with

spectsREFtargets20110408t2pcadfm =
melt(spectsREFtargets20110408t2pcadf,measure.vars=3:36)
qplot(value,data=spectsREFtargets20110408t2pcadfm,geom="text",label=target,color=target,facet=variable)

I want to plot all (or a subset of) PCs against each other using
ggplot or qplot.

Both datasets available here:
https://sites.google.com/site/filestemp2/home/spectsREFtargets20110408t2pcadfm.rda
https://sites.google.com/site/filestemp2/home/spectsREFtargets20110408t2pcadf.rda

Also, for the option with the 3 qplot(), would it be possible to put
the legend in the fourth corner?

Thanks

Agus

messages.subject: Re: Multiple PC plot with qplot or ggplot
parts:
Take the code and edit it. 

function (data, mapping = aes(), colour = "black") 
{
    grid <- expand.grid(x = 1:ncol(data), y = 1:ncol(data))
    grid <- subset(grid, x != y)
    all <- do.call("rbind", lapply(1:nrow(grid), function(i) {
        xcol <- grid[i, "x"]
        ycol <- grid[i, "y"]
        data.frame(xvar = names(data)[ycol], yvar = names(data)[xcol], 
            x = data[, xcol], y = data[, ycol], data)
    }))
    all$xvar <- factor(all$xvar, levels = names(data))
    all$yvar <- factor(all$yvar, levels = names(data))
    densities <- do.call("rbind", lapply(1:ncol(data), function(i) {
        data.frame(xvar = names(data)[i], yvar = names(data)[i], 
            x = data[, i])
    }))
    mapping <- defaults(mapping, aes_string(x = "x", y = "y"))
    class(mapping) <- "uneval"
    ggplot(all, mapping) + facet_grid(xvar ~ yvar, scales = "free") + 
        geom_point(colour = colour, na.rm = TRUE) + stat_density(aes(x = x, 
        y = ..scaled.. * diff(range(x)) + min(x)), data = densities, 
        position = "identity", colour = "grey20", geom = "line")
}
<environment: namespace:ggplot2>

I don't know if it is simpler but at least it should be easy to
transform into a function:

system("wget -O data.rda
https://sites.google.com/site/filestemp2/home/spectsREFtargets20110408t2pcadf.rda")
load("data.rda")
d = spectsREFtargets20110408t2pcadf
head(d)

# select a few PCs
PCsToPlot = 1:5
PCsToPlot = paste("PC",PCsToPlot, sep="")

# compute meaningful combinations
# NB: imbricated for loops are better than expand.grid() because
expand.grid() includes duplicates (i.e. 1 vs. 2 and 2 vs. 1)
nPC = length(PCsToPlot)
grid = matrix(ncol=2)
for (i in 1:(nPC-1)) {
for (j in (i+1):nPC) {
grid = rbind(grid, c(PCsToPlot[i], PCsToPlot[j]))
}
}
grid = grid[-1,] # remove the first row of NAs
head(grid)

# extract variables for all combinations
library("plyr")
ed = adply(grid, 1, function(x, d, extra) {
# extract PC values and extra identification variables
out = d[,c(extra,x)]
names(out) = c(extra, "x","y")
# identify what is x and what is y
out$PCx = x[1]
out$PCy = x[2]
return(out)
}, d=d, extra=c("target","type","grupos"))
head(ed)

# plot
library("ggplot2")
ggplot(ed) +
geom_hline(aes(yintercept=0), colour="white", size=1.5) +
geom_vline(aes(xintercept=0), colour="white", size=1.5) +
geom_point(aes(x=x, y=y, colour=grupos)) +
facet_wrap(~PCx+PCy, scales="free")
